utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel. If I could remind you of the affirmation which you took at the beginning of your evidence, it still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Petrovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojanovic. I'd like to pick up again where we left off yesterday. Yesterday, you told us that you had been assigned to the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. You told us that your unit was already in position by the time you took over command over the company. Can you please tell us where exactly was the unit positioned by the time you took over the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion, at the time when I took over command, was in the general area of Ivanica, which is a small town near the administrative border between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you arrive at Ivanica? When did you reach the place that your company was assigned to?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 21st of September, 1991, the same date that I reported to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember, please tell us, what sort of tasks was your company carrying out in the month of October 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the period between the time I took up my duty there on the 21st of September, 1991, and the beginning of October, this period was used to maintain manpower levels in the unit. And as I said yesterday, the unit did not have the manpower levels and did not have the men with adequate military occupational speciality. This situation continued until about the 1st of October, 1991, and then the 3rd Motorised Battalion, as soon as on the 1st of October started carrying out combat activities and engaged some Croatian units. I think it was some sort of a Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your company? Did they, too, take part in those combat operations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the combat disposition of the battalion, my company was on the left flank. Among other things, our task was to exercise control over the communication that runs between Bileca, Trebinje, and Dubrovnik. Therefore I was on the left flank of the battalion. I was providing security for the flank, and I did not directly take part in combat activities on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the battalion commander, the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade in October?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 21st of September, which was when I came, and the 1st of October, it was Captain First Class Ekrem Devlic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, was there a change at any point in time at the head of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 21st of October, this person that I referred to, Captain First Class Ekrem Devlic, was wounded and it was then that Captain -- Captain at the time Vladimir Kovacevic took over command of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, sometime in October was your battalion pulled out and sent for leave?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was in the first part of the month of October. We were pulled out to rest. I think the village was called Talez or Talezi. It was there. That's where the battalion was assigned, and we started our rest period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the month of November -- did you all this time in October and November 1991 stay -- keep your duty as the commander of the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion throughout this time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the time the battalion was pulled out and relocated to the village of Talezi for rest, I had some health problems. I had pneumonia, and in addition to the shots I was prescribed, the jabs, the doctor also sent me home for recovery. My family lived in Bileca at the time, and I was undergoing therapy there at the time. Therefore, I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you return to your position as commander of the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, I came back sometime early November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know if in the meantime your battalion or your company took part in any combat operations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion did take part in combat operations, and so did my company. On about the 15th, I found the unit in the Bosanka area. Combat operations were being carried out along the Brgat-Bosanka axis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned from sick leave, which specific positions was the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion holding at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period of time when I came back from sick leave, when I came back from home, I told you I found the company in the Bosanka area with two platoons that were deployed to the left, facing the sea, and there was another reinforced platoon and the remaining elements of the company with the command where the houses were in the village of Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can we show the witness P124, please. It's a map, a map of the unit's deployment on the 14th of November. Can we just please move the map so that we can see the area that we want to be looking at, that is the town of Dubrovnik itself and the immediate surroundings. If you can just move the map up a little. All right. I think we can see it clearly now. We can just zoom in a little, if possible, please. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you look at this map can you see the disposition of the units of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade? If so, please take the pointer and show us on the ELMO how the units were positioned. Above all, we're interested in the disposition of your unit, your company.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a relatively small scale map. It's a small scale map and I don't see it very clearly. However, these are the positions of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. Well, now here we have an alteration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, can you see the positions of your company here on this map?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see the positions of my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- can you point exactly where.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you have Bosanka, but I would like to make a remark here. Behind the unit you can see a sign, number 2, whereas in fact it should be 3, not 2, because it was the 3rd Motorised Company of the 3rd Motorised Battalion of the 472nd Brigade and not the 2nd. Therefore, where you see the number 2 there should in fact be number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we have seen the disposition of the units of the 3rd Battalion on the map, units of the 472nd Brigade, as in November, that's after you returned from sick leave. Tell us, sir, please, which units did the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade comprise?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade establishment-wise comprised the following units: The battalion command, three motorised companies; the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd. It had a mortar company. Those were 120-millimetre mortars. It had an anti-armour company. It had the Signals Unit, and it had a logistics platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to three motorised companies. In the period of time between your return from sick leave were all three motorised companies within the composition of the unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all three were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us which one wasn't and why?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Motorised Company was not within the composition at the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. time, and there was a reason. The reason was that the men we had who were part of the 1st Motorised Company, according to their military occupational speciality, were used to reinforce the 3rd Motorised Company at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell us again, please, you used those men to reinforce which motorised companies?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd and 3rd. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, in terms of weapons, what did your 3rd Motorised Company have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My company, the 3rd Motorised Company, had automatic rifles, 7.62 millimetres; machine guns, 7.62 millimetres, and sniper rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether any other weapons were added to your company, such as mortars or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no mortars. We had two T-55 tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when were these two T-55 tanks added to your company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those two tanks were added in the month of November. I can't specify the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which command those two tanks came from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came from our directly superior command, which is the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, was your battalion at any point in time reinforced with other weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion also had guns, so-called ZIS guns, 57 millimetres, so reinforcements came from our more superior command, the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the following document please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please tell us which command issued this document.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says so here in the heading that it's the command of the 472nd Motorised Brigade. That is their request for delaying a deadline and for resubordinating units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us who this document is addressed to and can we see from this document whether the addressee received the document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was sent to the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the original of this document, can you see anywhere a stamp showing that the 9th VPS received this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says the 22nd of November, 1991, the command of the 9th VPS. That's what it says on the stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the text in the middle of the B/C/S version. Under number 1 in the text itself. The rest is not relevant for what we are saying. Could you please take a look at number 1 and tell us what it is that the command of the 472nd Brigade is asking the commander of the 9th VPS do.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One, to send us a ZIS platoon urgently to join our unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is being requested from the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To have this platoon returned within the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the ZIS platoon that you referred to a few minutes ago, the one that was attached to the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the upper right-hand corner. What does it say in handwriting, and could you please read this out to us.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upper right-hand corner. First of all, I see: "To chief of staff. See/view possibilities" [as interpreted] if I can read that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it say further on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then in handwriting: "Resolve, approve not sending ZIS to Zaton, but do not approve taking ZIS platoon from the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade --" 472 period, that is "-- as long as the Srdj problem persists. Approve taking weapons from the SKL." That is probably warehouse Skladiste. Captain -- warship captain, Naval Captain Milan Zec signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I please tender this into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be D106.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said to us that your unit, your company, was deployed in the area of the village of Bosanka, and you explained to us a few minutes ago how it was deployed there. Tell us, please -- or, rather, could you describe the following to us: From the place where you commanded your company, that is to say from your observation post, what could you see? What are the features that you could see?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my observation post I could see Srdj, and if I were to look behind me, I could see Zarkovica as well. On the right I could see a bit of my neighbour towards Strincijera. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position, from your observation post, can the town of Dubrovnik be seen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The terrain has such geographic characteristics that I, from my position, would have to move about 250 or 300 metres minimum towards the sea in order to see the town. So that is what the terrain is like. So I could not notice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me briefly first, do you know who Miodrag Jokic is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miodrag Jokic, Admiral, is the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Gavro Kovacevic is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Gavro Kovacevic was Admiral Jokic's assistant commander for land forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of relationship existed between Admiral Jokic and Colonel Kovacevic on the one hand and Captain Kovacevic commander of one of your battalions on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say the following: Captain Vladimir Kovacevic before that, in peacetime, worked in the 472nd Motorised Brigade which was within the 9th Military Naval Sector. He knew these officers, especially Colonel Gavro Kovacevic, who was assistant commander for land forces. We had the impression, personal impression, as it were, that they highly trusted him as a soldier. They perhaps even looked up to him because of his qualities as a person and a soldier. So he did enjoy their trust.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Budimir Pesic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Budimir Pesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, who is this? Do you know where he was assigned, to which unit in the period from the 2nd of -- half of November to December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Budimir Pesic in that period, that is to say when he came after having accomplished certain tasks, he was within -- he was deployed in my company, but I do know the lieutenant from earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his duty within your company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period that we are talking about, the second half of November and December, the beginning of December 1991, were there any provocations launched against your company coming from the other side, the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was customary. They would fire from Srdj. So this called for additional efforts on the part of our personnel because it happened at different periods of time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone, to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the observation post where you were -- sir, the interpreters are asking you to come closer to the microphone so that they could hear you better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I took this position because I had spine surgery, so I have problems with my back. That's why I'm sitting this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. So from the position from where you commanded your company, what communications equipment did you have? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for communications equipment in the company, I had an RUP3, then an RUP12. And also there was a wire connection with the battalion command. That is to say the -- by using an M63 field telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, an RUP3, what is it used for?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a piece of communications equipment. RUP is radio receiver 3. It goes up to three kilometres, so it is for communication within a company. It's the company commander who communicates with platoon commanders within the company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about RUP12?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has a longer range, and it is used for communication between the company and the battalion. From the place where my observation post was, I could communicate with the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the telephone, the wire connection that you referred to, what is that used for?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also for communication between the company and the battalion. This wire connection is established by the communications platoon which, according to establishment, belongs to the battalion itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of communications equipment did the battalion have, or, rather, what kind of communications equipment existed, if you know, at the command post of the battalion itself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command post of the battalion itself, there was an RUP12, and the battalion commander communicated through it with his units within the battalion. So that is one type of communication. This is radio communication. Further on, we had a telephone switchboard, TCL10. That is to say that there can be ten participants involved in this switchboard. It is linked to the PTT cable and this field telephone, and that is how this kind of communication is established. Then a single -- a signalsman worked at that switchboard and that was used for communication between the battalion command and its -- and its subordinate unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please pause before putting his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] PTT is for civilian communications. PTK, PTK is for civilian communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, it is not clear now from what we can see. It is not clear in the transcript. So you said PTK cable. What is a PTK cable?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a two-prong capable with two different ends. One end goes into the switchboard and the other end goes into the field telephone. It is very simple to organise that kind of telephone communication, and it's a rather secure communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it only a military line of communication?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a line that cannot be eavesdropped on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned this communication at battalion command level and between the battalion command and the companies. Who else did the command of the 3rd Battalion communicate with through this equipment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's one more thing I wish to add. There was a messenger service that was organised too. So that was highly reliable. As for the battalion command, the battalion commander, in addition to other types of communication, in addition to the units that are within his own establishment, not to enumerate them all now, he had communication with his superior command, that is to say with the forward command post of the 9th Military Naval Sector in Kupari, down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this period in the second half of November and the beginning of December, were there any problems with the functioning of the communications system within your battalion and also between your battalion and the immediate superior command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, within your battalion how did command and reporting take place? Commanding, of course, on the part of the commander, and reporting, of course, from his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the battalion is headed by a battalion commander, and he is responsible for the general situation in the battalion. We commanders of companies, that is to say motorised companies and the anti-armour company and the 120-millimetre mortars company and the commander of the logistics platoon and of the signals platoon, we would report every day to the battalion commander. At this briefing at the battalion commander's, we would present the overall situation over the past 24 hours, and we would familiarise the commander with problems that may exist and seek assistance for carrying out certain tasks, if necessary, depending on the situation involved. So the commander within those 24 hours, every day through that briefing, he could receive information about the situation in his own unit, and in addition to that, by touring the units himself, he would obtain information as to what the situation was like and what the level of combat readiness was in each and every one of his subordinate units within the battalion, because he would have to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you came in in the middle of an interpretation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to ask the witness to slow down because I have received a message that nothing is recorded in the transcript. So that is the only thing I wanted to ask the witness to do, to slow down a bit so that we could have a proper transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a common purpose there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm just asking you to speak a bit slower, if possible, and to focus, please, on my questions so that we could finish as soon as possible in view of the time constraints that we have.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise for this. I said that every day we reported to the commander of the battalion about the overall situation in the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were these briefings held at the commander of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The briefings took place in the afternoon hours when the battalion commander would return from the briefing he would have at the forward command post in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander, the commander of the 3rd Battalion, inform you about the content of the briefings in Kupari and the tasks that he received in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he convey to you and inform you who it was who conducted the briefings at the forward command post in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who conducted these briefings in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The briefings in Kupari were conducted by the commander of the VPS, Admiral Jokic, or his deputy -- or, rather, the chief of staff, Milan Zec, Warship Captain Milan Zec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander convey to you the content of the orders that he received at these briefings in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he familiarise you with all the details that were presented at these briefings in Kupari that had something to do with your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander ever mention that he received certain assignments from the command of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, did he not mention any such thing because we were not within the 2nd Operational Group. We were within the 9th Military Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander mention that he had ever received a task in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, did you ever go for briefings to the forward command post in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went there twice for the briefings in Kupari. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us upon whose orders you went for the briefings there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the battalion commander's orders of Mr. Kovacevic, Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, these briefings in Kupari, where were they carried out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were carried out in Kupari at the forward command post in the operations room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to us, please, if you can, what the operations room was like at the time of the briefings and who attended these briefings at the time when you were there.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations room is a regular room. Apart from the furniture there, you have certain maps, indications, and on one side of the table there was a commander's seat, and around the table the commanders of subordinate units would be seated and those who were there from other commands and who were present at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you told us that you were twice present at these briefings. Could you tell us, please, the first time you were there, if you remember, who ran the briefings.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time, it was the Warship Captain Zec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he seated? Where was the person who chaired the briefing seated in relation to the others present there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would be seated at the head of the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned having gone there one other time. Who ran the briefing the second time you were there at the IKM in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second time the briefing was run by Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to explain to us how these briefings would take place; what they would start with, what their course would be, and how they would be ended.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief. Us commanders of subordinate units would report to the person running the briefing, whether the sector commander or his deputy chief of staff, we would report to him the general situation, order of the discipline in the units, provocations by the enemy. And this is what all commanders of subordinate units would speak about. Then the commanders of the organs of the sector; and then, depending on whether it was chief of staff or Admiral Jokic running the briefing, they would issue tasks to be carried out until the next briefing would take place. That would be the course of it, briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember those two times when you were in Kupari what it was that you stated about the situation in the unit? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would say where it was, along which axis that the Croats would be breaking the armistice, when and their disposition of the units, and I would also speak whether there was any need for us to engage any additional units from the command. So anything relating to realisation of our tasks and anything related to the day-to-day running of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us if you know whether the commander of your battalion or whoever he ordered to, whether he would be the one to go to Kupari regularly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is related to what you asked me earlier on. I told you that I went there twice on behalf of the battalion commander. He would otherwise go there regularly except for these few cases when he was prevented from doing so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the officers of the Military Naval Sector tour your units? And when I say "your units," I mean your company.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The deputy commander of the sector for land forces, Colonel Gavro Kovacevic, did. Then there were also those coming from the organs for political activity, for morale and moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would this visit by Colonel Kovacevic to your company look like?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as a company commander, would first of all report to Colonel Kovacevic and then I would briefly inform him about the general situation in the unit, primarily placing emphasis on the enemy situation, and then, according to his plan, we would be touring the units, and I'm speaking of my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned the command organ for morale. Could you just tell us in one sentence what this organ was about.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As its title says, it was an organ for political activity, for information and morale, for the information about the entire strength of the unit, of the unit and the general area, the measures undertaken by the unit to improve the situation, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you remember what this senior officer who was there before -- in front of the command -- on behalf of the command and who was in charge of political affairs and morale, what his name was?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was frigate captain. I don't know his name because I came from a different background and I didn't know the names of these different senior officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what this particular senior officer told you? What were the information that he conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us what the general situation was in the then Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, what the position of the army - that is of the Yugoslav People's Army - in that context was, the attack against Yugoslav People's Army, the impossibility to solve the political crisis in the state, the general situation in the area of responsibility of the 9th Military Naval Sector, and other such questions related to -- of relevance to the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this senior officer of the 9th VPS mention the events in the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember which ones?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To I as a soldier and other colleagues of mine, we were interested in the strength of the enemy, their head count, and where their firing points were in order for us to undertake adequate tactical measures and protect our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the document D53.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I would kindly ask you to take a look at the first paragraph of the document and to tell us whether the contents of this document tally with what the 9th VPS representative for political affairs and morale had conveyed to you during his visit to Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the first paragraph of the document before us, D53.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one day, the 3rd of November, 1991, where the members of the Croatian paramilitary formations, and that they opened fire and from which region at the JNA units, then the information that the sector command has at its disposal concerning the strength, that is the number of Croatian troops it has, it says here around 800 mercenaries in black shirts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not need this document any more. Mr. Stojanovic, were you ever at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can one see clearly the Old Town of Dubrovnik from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the very reason why I went to Zarkovica, to look at Dubrovnik, because one can see Dubrovnik from Zarkovica very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is approximately the distance between Zarkovica and the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, around two kilometres or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From such a distance can one distinguish a human figure, a vehicle, or any other facility as watching by naked eye?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it very well with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While being at that position, were you able to see any Croatian presence in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could, and I did from Zarkovica. I could see Croatian soldiers on the move with long barrels. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of the town of Dubrovnik did you see Croatian soldiers with long barrels?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, among other places, also in the old part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these briefings that were carried out at the command of your battalion, were you informed about any other forms of Croatian -- of Croatian military presence in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There -- there was information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about these pieces of information about the Croatian military presence in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the type of information that contained in the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. This is clearly outside the summary with which we were provided, inadequate as it was, as was indeed the information the witness provided a moment ago about Croatian soldiers. That wasn't in the summary. The Prosecution objects to this evidence being led without proper notice to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a moment, please. In the summary provided by us to the OTP on the 11th of July, it says that in the period of November and December he had seen persons armed with long barrels in the Old Town of Dubrovnik. That's what's stated in the summary on the 11th of July, 2004, and I hope that my learned colleague has received it. First of all, in -- when I look at your instructions, Your Honour, I cannot see that this goes beyond the scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're now asking not about anything seen by this witness but what he might have been told about Croatian forces, and the objection is that that is quite outside anything of which there was notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they have been informed about him having to testify about the contents of the briefings, and if we're talking about the contents of the briefings, well, then this forms part of it. But such an approach taken by my learned colleagues would require us to really take the witness's statement and to deliver every single sentence of what he's going to testify about here, and this is something that we cannot provide. We believe that the information we provided was sufficient, and what the witness is saying now is something that he heard. It's not something that he saw but that he heard from others. And I do not really see that there is any difficulty in this, but of course I will abide by Your Honour's instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is nothing in the "summary" that we received at 7.30 on Sunday night about Croatian soldiers. It was about persons with long-barrelled -- there is nothing about information about Croatian weaponry in the Old Town or near the Old Town. There is nothing about briefings. There is nothing about this witness meeting Admiral Jokic. There is nothing about him meeting Captain Zec. It is in the vaguest and most general terms. The Prosecution is unable to prepare for cross-examination if we don't know a basic summary of the facts. A fact would be "attended briefings with Jokic." We don't even have that much less the content of those briefings. This is going way beyond the two-paragraph vague generalised summary that this witness was -- well, apparently in Zarkovica because it doesn't really say that either. That's another point, that the summary -- none of the three -- the three different paragraphs we have got even mentions the witness was at Zarkovica. Again it's way outside. I didn't object, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Mr. Petrovic, I think the point now is reaching too far from the summary, but in any event, it's going to be evidence of very little weight to the Chamber to hear what this witness might have been told by some people, unspecified, at different times about troop movements. So we'll leave that subject and move on to something else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I've understood you correctly, you are instructing me to simply leave out whatever it was that the witness had heard from others concerning the Old Town and what he had heard during the briefings of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'd thought we'd covered the briefings in some detail, and that's happened without objection. But you're now asking him specifically about troops, Croatian forces, what he might have been told about those. That's the subject that is too far. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we'll move on to our last subject. Tell us, sir -- we'll move on to events in December 1991, more specifically the 5th of December, 1991. On that day did you hear anything about negotiations that were afoot or about a peace agreement that had been signed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard no such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the briefing that was held on the 5th of December, 1991, at the positions of your company and your battalion, was there anything unusual or out of the ordinary going on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing usual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you called in for a briefing on that day in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who it was that called you, and what exactly were you told?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was called by the duty officer who was manning the switchboard. The assignment I was given was to see the battalion commander for a briefing, and the company commanders would then go there and wait for the commander who was elsewhere on a different mission, and then there would be a briefing once he returned from Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm really not sure what the transcript says. I didn't hear that in B/C/S. Therefore, I must ask you again, and can you please carefully and slowly repeat your answer, because there's simply something you didn't say in Serbian. Who called you and what did they tell you? So can this section of the tape please be checked later. Who was it who called you to come to the briefing and what exactly were you told?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was called by the duty communications officer who was at the battalion command. Secondly, he conveyed to me an order saying that my task was to report to the Ivanica area, to a house in that area where we would then wait for the battalion commander who was on his way from a briefing that had been held at Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Who was present at the briefing at the battalion commander that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the unit commanders from the 3rd Battalion were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the battalion commander arrive?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, the company commanders, were already there at the place that was assigned, and the battalion commander, the Commander Lemal was among the last to arrive because he was the most distant, and then after him Captain Kovacevic, the battalion commander, arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Captain Kovacevic come from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, as usual, Captain Kovacevic had gone to the forward command post in Kupari for a briefing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Captain Kovacevic tell you that he had been assigned a task there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say? What did Captain Kovacevic say? What sort of a mission was he assigned or, rather, his battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that Admiral Jokic, the commander, had given him the task to move on to Srdj and attack Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he speak about any details concerning this attack on Srdj that had been ordered?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had his working notebook, and he used it to remind himself so he could give us unit commanders the details about that particular mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he use that notebook to read out specific tasks in respect of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. each single unit that was within the battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him any questions? I mean Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what exactly you asked.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was familiar with the area, and I knew what the task was that he had given me, so I wanted him to explain the issue of fire support. It's an open area, Srdj was above the defence of my unit, and that's why I needed a lot of preparation in terms of fire support. I asked who would be providing that support for the units later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did Captain Kovacevic tell you? Who would be providing fire support for the battalion during the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlado said at the time that 130-millimetre battery would do that because they were in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the objective of this attack that was explained to you by Vladimir Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective was to take Srdj quickly, to hold onto that position and continue to exercise control over that territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the taking of Srdj, did Vladimir Kovacevic mention any other objective, perhaps an attack on Dubrovnik or something like that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were specific tasks divvied up to other units that were part of the company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Specific tasks were given to all the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which task was your unit assigned?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My company, the 3rd Motorised Company, got the task to take one assault group and to carry out an assault and attack along the Bosanka Srdj access.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to carry out this task that you'd been given, did you request any equipment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What specifically did you request?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I requested some equipment that we needed, bulletproof vests in order to protect my men who were about to launch the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this briefing with the battalion commander, where did you go next? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already dark and we were in a hurry to get back to the unit. I went back to Bosanka, and I set about organising that particular task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the evening or at any other point in time were you in fact given the equipment that you had requested from the battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After organising the attack once I had assigned my men to the task, I had a rest. We needed to get some rest, so we laid down. There was an arduous task awaiting the next day. During the night, I received a call from Zarkovica to report there in order to take over the equipment that I had requested. So I did report and I did in fact take over the equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact start implementing the task that you had been given the evening before by the battalion commander, Vladimir Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We received this task on the 5th of December, and we started implementing the task in the morning hours on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, when did this group from your company start carrying out the task?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was after the fire preparation of the attack which just started at about 5.00 in the morning. So the group set out eventually at about 6.00 in the morning. Sir, Mr. Petrovic, if I can please request a short break since my back is starting to hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, do you think we could possibly have a short break now, because the witness appears to be suffering some health problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will break for 20 minutes now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, can we now proceed with this examination? You feel fine, I hope?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the last thing we mentioned was that the attack began at around 6.00 in the morning. Do you know, roughly speaking, how the attack was organised, bearing in mind all the groups that were to take part in the attack? Do you know along which axes these groups were supposed to launch this attack on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My task was to use the assault group, that is for my unit to attack along the axis of a group of houses in the Bosanka village, a quarry at the foot of Srdj, and the feature of Srdj itself. On the right flank of the battalion Captain Lemal had a company there with two assault groups along that axis, the Strincijera-Srdj axis, and to attack along the flank and to coordinate with me as soon as Srdj was reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who led this group, the group from your company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That group was led by Lieutenant Budimir Pesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your observation post did you follow the operation of Budimir Pesic's assault group?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were watching from the observation post. My messenger was there as well as my signals officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Pesic's group proceed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once they carried out the fire preparations for the attack, Lieutenant Pesic headed out with his group. He started the attack, and the attack progressed as we had envisaged it. So as they were moving towards the target, from the Dubrovnik area fire was opened from anti-aircraft guns. So he had to use the dead angles in order to avoid suffering any casualties. And I was watching this from my observation post. I had already reached my observation post by 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Pesic's group succeed in approaching the Srdj feature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and they reached the Srdj feature and then close range fighting began from artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: From infantry weapons, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say -- Your Honours, we have a problem. The interpretation says on page 30, line 7, from artillery weapons whereas the witness said from infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stojanovic, you said that as soon as Pesic reached Srdj, fighting began using infantry weapons. Who engaged whom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We engaged Croatian soldiers who were deployed along the plateau on top of Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, roughly speaking, at what time Pesic's group reached the Srdj feature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had started out at about 6.00, so it was past 8 that he reached Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout this attack, were you in contact with the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point in time did you receive any information from the battalion command in connection with Officer Pesic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was about half past eight that I received information that Lieutenant Pesic had been wounded, seriously wounded in fact, to the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do once you had received that information?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I received that information I took a group of about ten Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. soldiers, we got onto a Pinzgauer vehicle and took the path to the Srdj feature to pull Lieutenant Pesic out to try to have him evacuated. So the assault group was without their commander that time, and I went there to take over command of the unit at Srdj because I was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time elapsed before you were able to reach Srdj itself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drove in that vehicle, and I also had to take advantage of the dead angles, in military lingo. I had to move along that axis so as to avoid casualties inflicted by anti-aircraft fire from Dubrovnik itself. After I left the vehicle, I took over an hour to actually reach the feature of Srdj itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once there, what did you find there at the Srdj feature itself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I had to literally crawl on all fours with that group, the people who were with me, to reach Srdj. There were -- there was a metal staircase there, and with the support of my forces that were there at Srdj, I came out and I took shelter, which is where Sergeant Tuka Miralem briefly familiarised me with the situation. There was a lot of hand-to-hand combat going on using infantry weapons, hand grenades, pistols. I took over command and naturally, as any soldier would do, I tried to inflict as many losses on the enemy in terms of human lives as I could, and I tried to calm the confusion that was raging within the ranks. You know the sort of thing that can happen once a unit commander is wounded and out of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how exactly Officer Pesic was wounded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Pesic had taken shelter at Srdj. It was a kind of shelter. It was actually a fridge used to store ice cream. So he took shelter behind that fridge, and he was hit by shrapnel in his helmet, and then he had a head wound that was very serious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Sergeant Miralem? Did he tell you anything about the progress of fighting, how far they got fighting the Croatian crew that was stationed at Srdj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us that on account of the heavy firing from the infantry weapons by the group that was there, the Croatian soldiers were trying to surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the feature, were you under fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did come under fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what sort of fire it was that you came under.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this mortar fire was coming from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the left flank, from the direction of Dubrovnik, but I can't give you the exact position of the weapon because I couldn't see it from the Srdj feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the members of the assault group from your company? Was there anyone else except for Pesic who was wounded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the attack on Srdj, an active-duty soldier from Pirat was killed and three of the reserve privates were also seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As at one point you came under mortar fire, did you request artillery support for your unit that was at the Srdj feature by that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I requested, of course, that they step up the firing and that they use 130-millimetre guns. That was, after all, part of our assignment. It said that we would be receiving support from guns, guns that would be firing at those features or targets in Dubrovnik that were firing at us and that were inflicting losses on our troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the Srdj feature for?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For over an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive the artillery support that had been promised?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether your unit could have held out at Srdj without this artillery support?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Had I known there would be no artillery support, I certainly would not have accepted any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you decide after you realised there was no artillery support and after your unit sustained these losses at Srdj itself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, as there was this strong mortar fire, after Pesic was wounded and after this active-duty soldier was killed and others wounded, and since there was no support, I as commanding officer decided to leave that position and to get my personnel out. I was simply compelled to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consult anyone regarding this decision to withdraw from Srdj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not consult anyone. This was my own estimate and my own decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After how much time did you manage to get back to your basic position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, from 9.00 on I was at Srdj for a bit over an hour, and then of course I had to take measures because retreating from that position is not mere flight. One group gets out, another group gives its support. So it took me about two hours to withdraw from there. So it was past midday. It was 1300 or 1400 hours by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you and your soldiers, did you withdraw from Srdj at your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, the 6th of December, were you ordered at any point to stop the attack at Srdj, the one that your company was carrying out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, the order to attack Srdj that was issued the previous day, was it revoked at any point while you and your soldiers were at Srdj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it had not been revoked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the previous day, were you and your colleagues given some other task except for the task to take Srdj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only the task of taking Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The evening before, at the briefing on the 5th of December, was any activity planned in terms of firing at the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a specific objective, only if there would be an objective that would be lethal for the unit itself, as was proved to be true in the case of the unit that was at Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Is it Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It is indeed, thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just on that last point, Mr. Stojanovic, in which you said there was a briefing the day before, that was the briefing conducted by Mr. Kovacevic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was the -- to be quite clear on this, you as the company commander received your orders only from Kovacevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No one else issued orders to you directly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you're saying, that no one else issued orders directly to you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this military hierarchy, it's only the battalion commander that can issue orders to me because I was a company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of military hierarchy, that of course goes up, Kovacevic to his superior, and that person's superior, and so on to the very top?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that point I'm only interested in the line between the company and the battalion. That is to say I myself and Vladimir Kovacevic. I as a company commander am not interested in the chain of command any further. I'm not interested in what anybody superior to Vladimir Kovacevic thinks at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're saying you're not interested, are you saying you're Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. unaware or you took no interest in who Kovacevic's superiors were?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm interested in the unit that is under my command, and I'm interested in carrying out tasks that are given to me by the battalion commander. In this specific case, Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to go back to what I was asking you and that was the state of your knowledge. Was it the fact that you were uninterested in who Kovacevic's superiors were or you were unaware of who his superiors were, that is who he took orders from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did know who Vladimir Kovacevic's superior officer was. That was Admiral Jokic. As for the relationship between Captain Kovacevic and Admiral Jokic, in military terms it is not for me to look into that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling this Tribunal you were unaware of who Jokic's superior was in November and December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you asked me who Jokic's superior officer was, or are you asking me who Kovacevic's superior officer was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've just told us that as far as you were concerned, Kovacevic -- sorry, Jokic was Kovacevic's superior, but then you said as to who was Jokic's -- I'm sorry. What I'm asking you -- I withdraw that last point. What I'm asking you is were you aware in October -- sorry, in November and December 1991 of who Jokic's superior was.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jokic, Admiral Jokic, was commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector. I was not interested in the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You attended, you told us yesterday, the elite military training academy at Bileca, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the things they teach you there is subordination from bottom to top, don't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The chain of command in this specific case goes from me, commander of the 3rd Motorised Company. My immediate superior is Captain Vladimir Kovacevic. As we go further up the chain of command, his superior officer and mine is Admiral Jokic as the commander of the 9th Military Naval Sector. As for Commander Jokic, his superior is the commander of the Military Naval District, and all the way up to the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army. I believe that you have understood my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When a commander of any rank issues an order, in that order they can name a superior who has given that order, can't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to repeat your question. The interpretation is coming very fast, and these are questions that have to be dealt with slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In issuing an order, a commander can and will, in that order, say who has given him that order.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this specific case. I told you that this order was received by Captain Vladimir Kovacevic, who was battalion commander. I -- his superior, Admiral Jokic, gave him his orders according to this hierarchy, if you are referring to this specific case, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking only in general terms from what you learnt in your military training and putting it into practice, and that is, in general terms, when a commander issues an order, the commander can refer to who has given him that order. What I'm saying is, in an order, a commander can refer to an order from above, can't he. Such as "pursuant to an order from the general secretary of defence," or "pursuant to an order from another general, I am issuing you this order."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part -- well, let me tell you. In that period, I was a lower-ranking commander. Companies, platoons, I was not interested in these higher levels of command at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Admiral Jokic issues orders saying that he has received orders from General Strugar, because you're not interested in that level of the functioning of hierarchy, you wouldn't be able to disagree with it, would you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your question. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've said you weren't interested in the hierarchy. Who was above Jokic in the hierarchy? So if Jokic has issued orders in which he has said he has received those orders from General Strugar or his predecessor as the head of the 2nd Operational Group, you wouldn't be able to disagree -- you couldn't disagree with Jokic saying that he was issuing those orders pursuant to higher orders from General Strugar, would you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Jokic could not receive orders from General Strugar in any event because he was not subordinated to General Strugar. He was subordinated to the then commander of the Military Naval District. General Strugar had a completely different duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would accept, sir, that General -- sorry, Admiral Jokic would be in a much better position to say who he was receiving his orders from than you, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that. You'll have to ask Admiral Jokic that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting you would be in a better position than Admiral Jokic to say who he was receiving orders from, sir?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If Jokic says he was receiving orders from Strugar in orders issued to the 472nd, you couldn't disagree with that, could you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in which context you are mentioning this link between Admiral Jokic and General Strugar to me here. For a then company commander, that was not the kind of thing that a person like that would think about. Everybody knows what a company commander is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've made a statement to the Tribunal earlier that your company was not within the 2nd Operational Group. Do you remember giving that evidence earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which period you're referring to when you say "earlier".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier today and yesterday, you told the Tribunal that your company and your battalion was not within the 2nd Operational Group, if I understand your evidence correctly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said yesterday that I was commander of the 3rd Company of the 3rd Motorised Battalion, which was under the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector. The sector was headed by Admiral Jokic. I don't know what other statement you may be referring to. In my testimony, I did not mention the 2nd Operational Group at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would Your Honour excuse me for just one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The note we have - I don't have the transcript directly in front of me at the moment - is your saying earlier today that the commander never said he received orders from the 2nd Operational Group, in response to a question from Mr. Petrovic, "because we were not part of the 2nd Operational Group." I'm just reminding you that's what you said earlier today. Does that jog your memory as to what you said maybe an hour ago to Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, what you said just now, I mean, I don't see where we differ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Strugar was the commander of the 2nd Operational Group in November and December 1991. Can we agree on that? Also October 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that General Strugar was the commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your evidence that your company was within the 2nd Operational Group or not within the 2nd Operational Group? Which one is it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my company was within the 3rd Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out whether you're saying the ultimate subordination was to the 2nd Operational Group or to somewhere else. What do you say? If you don't know, just -- just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if you are familiar with our military hierarchy, then you know what the command situation was in the then Yugoslav People's Army. Then you know that that was the upward chain of command. I'm a company commander. My unit is within a battalion. The battalion operated under the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector. So that is the chain that I was interested in as company commander and that was of relevance to my unit. This level of command, that is to say a company commander, fully relies on the command of the battalion and receives orders from the commander of the battalion. In this case, I received orders from my colleague, my superior officer, Captain Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't know, please just tell the Trial Chamber you don't know. Do you know whether General Strugar -- sorry, whether Admiral Jokic was subordinated to General Strugar or not, that is to the 2nd Operational Group. If you don't know, just please tell the Trial Chamber you don't know.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic was not subordinated to General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would accept, wouldn't you, that if General Strugar is issuing orders to Admiral Jokic and Admiral Jokic is obeying those orders, that would suggest he was subordinated, Jokic was subordinated to Strugar, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a twofold issue and is of no significance to me. This was, after all, a higher level of command that I could not possibly be interested in, if you understand me correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've given some evidence about subordination, and you've just told the Trial Chamber that Jokic was not subordinated to Strugar. You are a serving senior officer in the army, in the military. Now, if Strugar was issuing orders to Jokic and Jokic was obeying them and passing them on, that can only mean that Jokic was subordinated to Strugar, can't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
