Again I'm without a diary, not having anticipated that this was the issue to be raised, but we were thinking the first Monday and Tuesday of September for final oral submissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I ask a question of the Chamber? Issues of rebuttal are being looked at. The situation for the Prosecution has been, as the Chamber is aware, that what we believe a witness may say and what may ultimately come up during examination has not necessarily been the same. Does the 23rd reflect any possible rebuttal or is that a conclusion of the Defence evidence? Was there a contemplation for a day or so after that for any possible rebuttal, the need for which is still up in the air depending on how things materialise with the way the case has been going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The following Monday and Tuesday are spare days. The Wednesday is not because the Tribunal has Plenary sittings on Wednesday and Thursday, but not the Monday and Tuesday. So if there was need for further evidence, it could be accommodated then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do I understand with two days allotted for closing arguments that it is a day per side? Is that the contemplated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unless you are to finish very quickly and allow the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: As I was saying, a day per side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you see, it is in addition to detailed written submissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it wouldn't be a matter of rereading those but of dealing with highlights, high points, and perhaps some observations on the written submissions of the other party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. My colleagues have informed me that we have been informed by the Defence of their expectation to call the experts the 23rd through the 30th, so I think with the Chamber's having just made this announcement, the Defence, I guess, will have to reallocate its time a little bit differently. We didn't realise the -- I -- when I asked you I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have heard nothing other than that the Defence case will take no longer than four weeks, and that is Friday the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've actually now been allocating extra sitting hours this week and next week to try and ensure that there is every opportunity to the Defence to deal with their evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And certainly the Chamber is not available after Tuesday of the week following because of the Plenaries. Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: One last question: It is not known whether or not the Chamber is contemplating a site visit of any kind. If the Chamber is so contemplating, we would be grateful to -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, as the evidence has progressed, I've got to say our expectation has grown that if not the Prosecution, certainly the Defence would be of the view that there needs to be a site visit to understand some of this evidence, and if that were the case, it would probably be preferable for the site visit to be interposed between the written submissions and the final oral submissions so that the final oral submissions could take account of the site inspection. That would mean probably deferring for some few days, at least, the oral submissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for the indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But we've just been conscious of how much the evidence now seems to depend on capacities to see, distances and times of movement from various locations, and I think the way things are going, the Chamber would not be at all surprised if either or both parties were of the view that an inspection is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. It had been contemplated indeed earlier and there have been some informal discussions, but it had not arrived at the level you just mentioned. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anything, Mr. Rodic, that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as my learned friend said just now, we have discussed this between the parties, that is to say the final submissions and when this could take place. The date of the 23rd or around the 23rd of August was mentioned. Of course both parties, as far as I could understand, addressed the registrar in terms of whether we could move the date forward seven days. The parties agreed it would be good if it could be postponed for seven days because it is holiday season, there is lots of work, and then there are family problems and obligations involved on the part of certain individuals. At any rate, we would appreciate it if the deadline could be postponed by seven days, but of course this is ultimately in the hands of the Honourable Trial Chamber. As for this particular piece of information relating to the 28th and 29th of July, as you said just now, the Trial Chamber will be busy then on account of the Plenaries, and we know that this is an important annual commitment, although the Defence was not aware of the actual dates. We were talking about four weeks, and we hope -- or, rather, we shall make every effort to conclude the Defence case within that period of time, with a possible reservation that it could certainly be completed by Wednesday, the 28th of July when you say that the Trial Chamber is busy with the Plenary Session here at the Tribunal. The Defence is going to call its expert witnesses next week. They will arrive in The Hague. In order to fit into the schedule, if so need be, we may give up on one witness or two. I cannot say anything more specific now, but taking into account the actual schedule, perhaps we could resort to that. There is another question that our client raised with us as a problem, and that is precisely the new schedule according to which we work, starting at 9.30 until 4.30 p.m. That means that he is in the Tribunal for seven hours and at least one hour before that and one hour after that. The general has complained to us that, in view of his health condition, he cannot really take this. This is a major difficulty for him spending such a long period of time here in the Tribunal. That is what the Defence wished to say in relation to the subjects that have been raised. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic. Dealing with those different matters, first, one overall concern of the Chamber is to prevent this trial dragging out unnecessarily, precisely out of concern for your client and his health and to try to reach the point where there can be a final decision as soon as possible, because I think we can all appreciate that nothing will be more draining on him than the ongoing anxiety of not knowing where this trial will get to. We remain in the expectation that it should be possible to conclude the evidence for the Defence by the end of sitting on Friday, the 23rd of July, and we will proceed on that basis. If there is some rearrangement of sitting hours that would be more convenient but which would still enable us to get about an extra hour a day, we would certainly be prepared to hear from you on that once you've had a chance to consider it, but we're trying to find this extra time to try to give you more time for dealing with your evidence than you had indicated you needed, because clearly we were slipping behind your schedule. So we'll leave that as it is at the present time, but you may raise it again if you see some way of improving the position. The Chamber will look at your submission that we might defer the written submissions by perhaps a week. In part that would fit in with the question whether or not there should be a site inspection, but again we make the point that will simply prolong the trial from your client's point of view. So there are perhaps some things now for counsel on each side to think about to see where we are, but I hope at the moment the present understanding and intentions of the Chamber are clear, and their objective is to try to ensure that as quickly as is possible, consistently with fairness, we can bring the trial to its proper conclusion in the interests of your client. We should now hear the witness who is waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence calls Budimir Pesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, I have to point out, Your Honour, that the preparation of this witness has not been completed, and we have not concluded our proofing. At the moment when the witness was summoned to appear before the Honourable Trial Chamber, the witness was having lunch. So he cut his lunch short, but we did not conclude the proofing session that would certainly have been important in terms of preparing this witness properly for his evidence before this Honourable Trial Chamber. Of course the Defence never questions the decisions of the Honourable Trial Chamber, and this particular time is no exception to that. Allow me to start, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Good afternoon, Mr. Pesic. Would you be kind enough to stand and read the affirmation that will be given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Petrovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pesic, please tell us for the transcript your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: My name is Budimir Pesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your profession is.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I'm a professional military man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were born.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I was born in Kosovska Vitina, the municipality of Kosovska Vitina in Kosovo, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us what schools you completed, sir.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I completed the military academy, the land forces department infantry in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did your schooling at the academy last?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: For four years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when have you been in professional military service in the Yugoslav People's Army or now the army of Serbia and Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: In the then Yugoslav People's Army, I started my professional service in the month of August 1987.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, at this point in time, where are you serving?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: At this point in time I'm at the Presevo garrison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What rank do you hold, Mr. Pesic?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I'm a major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to wait a few moments for the interpretation to be recorded in the transcript. So let us pause between my question and your answer so that everything would be reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon completing the military academy, where was your first post?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Upon completing the military academy in 1987, my first post was in the school of reserve officers in Bileca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties at the reserve officers school in Bileca?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I was commanding officer of the cadets platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you serve in the course of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: From the month of July 1991, I served in the Naval Landing Brigade in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this come about? How were you transferred from the reserve officers school in Bileca to the Naval Landing Brigade in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I received orders for this transfer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when this order was issued, approximately?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that I was transferred to Trebinje sometime in mid-July 1999, and I received this order towards the end of September the same year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Trebinje, were you assigned to a specific unit?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Trebinje, I started taking over the duties of company commander in the 3rd Battalion, but the following day, with a unit, I received orders to go to Split to provide security for the Kozjak feature, which was five kilometres away from Split.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you secure this feature in the surroundings of Split?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I remained there until the 30th of October, 1991, at which time I returned to my home unit in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the assignment and upon whose orders were you sent to secure this feature near Split?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I was sent by oral orders of the commander of the brigade of the naval landing marines. I think that he was a colonel, and his name was Nojko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the specific order given by Nojko Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: My orders were to be prepared with my men for a certain task. I didn't know what the task specifically was to be. We were told that we would be transported in helicopters to the location where we would receive more specific orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Marinovic explain to you the purpose of your assignment in the context of the general situation in the country at the time?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel -- was Colonel Marinovic at the head of the Naval Landing Brigade after you returned from your task?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't at the head of this brigade. I received information that he had fled the army and moved to Dubrovnik. And at that time when I returned, he was the commander of the defence of Dubrovnik or, rather, the forces who were at the time in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you surprised by the fact that the officer who had sent you to a certain assignment was not any longer with the unit at the time when you returned from your mission?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Not especially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon your return from Split or, rather, from the surroundings of Split, where did you go? To which unit did you go to?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Upon my return from Split on the 30th of October, 1991, I was granted a seven-day leave, which I spent at home in Kosovo, and after that I was assigned to the 1st Platoon of the 3rd Company of the 3nd Battalion of the naval landing forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the 1st Platoon of the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion of the Naval Landing Brigade, do you know -- can you give us any more specific assignment? Designation of this unit, any numbers.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: That is its official name; the 1st Platoon of the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the numerical designation of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember that. At the moment I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your unit stationed at the moment when you were assigned, or appointed, rather, the commander of the 1st Platoon of the 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: It was in the area of Brgat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who sent you there to the unit upon your return from Split?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I was assigned there by the personnel organ of the brigade of the Naval Marine Brigade. I think it was on the 8th of November, 1991, but I'm not sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this unit subsequently involved in combat operations after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: After my arrival, my unit was involved on the night between 9th and 10th - and I'm talking about the time when I came to the unit - in the area around the villages Bosanka and Srdj, and it was also involved on -- in combat on Srdj on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the battalion that you were assigned to?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion was Captain Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the company that you were assigned to?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The company commander was Captain Slavoljub Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the witness to be shown Exhibit P124, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pesic, do you recognise this area which is shown in the map?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please let me finish the question first. What is this area?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: This is the Dubrovnik hinterland. It's the territory in and around Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see on this map the positions of the 3rd Battalion of the -- of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see the positions of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade of the naval marines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This designation 472 is a numerical designation of the brigade that you were part of or a member of at the time?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I couldn't remember at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please take a pointer and show on this map, but not on the monitor but on the ELMO itself. So can you see on this map the positions of the firing group of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I see the firing positions in the area of Uskoplje of the 3rd Battalion of the Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which firing pieces were part of the firing group?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: They had 120- and 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the deployment of the unit of the 3rd Battalion, can you see motorised companies as well?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, the 3rd Company that you were a member of, was its position of deployment correctly displayed on this map?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: It is not correctly marked on the map. The 3rd Company was in the area of Bosanka village, whereas in the map it says that this was the position of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on the map the positions of anti-armour company?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The anti-armour company was on the Zarkovica feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see, as marked on this map, the enemy positions? If you can, can you show them to us.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I see the enemy unit positions, and according to my information and observation, they were deployed from the Belvedere Hotel at the entrance point to Dubrovnik all the way down to Mokosica, Babin Kuk, and Dubrovnik itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us on the map the position of the units on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: There were ZNG units on Srdj. That's the Croatian National Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We don't need this map any more. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned that you were involved in the operations on the 6th of December, 1991. Where were you positioned on the 5th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: On the 5th December 1991, I was stationed in the village of Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One moment, please. Was the whole company that you were a member of stationed in Bosanka village?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally on that day given any kind of an assignment?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: From my company commander, Captain Stojanovic, on the night between the 5th and the 6th, I was given an assignment to take part of my platoon and become involved in the taking hold of the Srdj feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you receive this assignment from your company commander?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I received the assignment in the area of Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the idea underpinning this operation of taking hold of the Srdj feature?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I can explain what my mission and what my role was to be within the forces that were engaged in this operation since only my men from my company were engaged for this operation of taking hold of this specific feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what was your specific assignment?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: My assignment was to -- in dawn of the 6th of December, 1991, with some elements of my company and with the support of the mortars from the battalion firing group, 130-millimetre guns and a T-55 tank as support, to take hold of one section of the Srdj feature along the axis Bosanka village, along the road -- asphalt road, and the repeater which was positioned on the very feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The attack that you received an order for the evening before, was it actually carried out the following day?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the attack commence and how?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The attack commenced at around 0600 hours with the activity of the battalion fire group from the area of Uskoplje firing upon Srdj. That is, it started with the preparation of the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the preparation of fire, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The units that were designated to take part in the attack launched the attack in a successive manner, depending on how far their starting position was away from the feature, so that not all the units set out at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you personally at the time when the attack commenced?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I was at my starting position some 700 metres away from Srdj in the direction of the village of Bosanka. That is the axis of the village of Bosanka-Srdj along the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you head out toward the Srdj feature at some point during the day?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: With my unit, I set out toward the Srdj feature at 6.20 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember, that morning, what was the agreed sign for the commencement of the activities against the Srdj feature? What was the signal?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I received the order to start the attack from my commander of the company, and I don't know at the level of the battalion what the signal, what the agreed signal was for the start of the preparation of the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you set out towards the Srdj feature after having completed the firing preparation. What was your advance towards Srdj like?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: At the time I started advancing towards Srdj the preparation was still in course because we were at such a distance from the feature that it permitted the activity of the mortars. I set out with a tank and some of my men with some 12 to 14 troops, and after having passed some 200 to 300 metres in the direction of the feature, we were fired upon from an 82-millimetre mortar, that is precisely two 82-millimetre mortars, who were firing from the area of Babin Kuk, that is, more precisely, from the area of the tennis fields -- tennis courts. In my estimate, fire was opened also from the Old Town and from an anti-aircraft machine-gun because I noticed the bullets --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're outside of any notice that's been provided to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. In what respects?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just as he -- just as he's starting to talk about "In my estimate fire was also opened" - so it looks like an assumption - "from the Old Town and from an anti-aircraft gun because I noticed bullets." So as soon as we start getting to -- Actually, all of the discussion here, the Babin Kuk, from the tennis fields, from the tennis courts, the estimate the fire was also opened from the Old Town in his estimate, the anti-aircraft, that's outside the 65 ter summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would suggest that you continue with your examination Mr. Petrovic. The evidence will be heard subject to the objection, and we'll see where it leads.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to note that my learned colleague would have received a supplement to all the information as we used to do it so far had it not been for the present circumstances where we were unable to deliver such a document. Thank you, Your Honours. I will continue with my examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pesic, you mentioned that in your estimate you were fired upon from the direction of the Old Town. Can you tell us, what was it exactly that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I notice tracer bullets flying over us from that direction. I'm not claiming that fire was opened from the Old Town, I'm just saying that it came from that direction. And the mortars in the -- and the mortar in the area of the tennis court was seen by my observer and by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, therefore, observed the fire that was opened against your unit, and that was, in your estimate at the time, coming from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: It was hitting behind and to the left of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the specific evidence of the witness was it was from the direction of the Old Town. He specifically said he did not claim it came from the Old Town. Your question put it from the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the interpretation is not precise. I'm talking about the direction of the Old Town. My question referred to the direction from the Old Town, and this can be checked from the tape that this is being recorded to, and I'm sorry for any possible unclarities that might arise from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Petrovic. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pesic, which weapons were held by your assault group to -- which was given the assignment to seize this feature of Srdj?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: We had automatic rifles, hand grenades, hand-held rocket launchers of 64 millimetres, Zoljas, and I had the AGF grenades which were intended for repelling riots which had agents affecting physiologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which purposes would these AGF grenades be used for?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Well, when the tasks are being carried out in certain premises, because we were told at the Srdj feature there were tunnels and the like, and these grenades were primarily intended for hitting these targets in tunnels and closed areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which direction you took from the village of Bosanka. You personally, not your unit.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: I was taking the left side of the asphalt road going from Bosanka, that is sumarak [phoen], pine wood, towards the Srdj feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your action did you use any armour weapons?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: We had the support of a T-55 tank that was within my group's establishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which direction did the tank T-55 advance?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: For a while it took the asphalt road, and then some 200 to 300 metres in front of the Srdj feature it would -- it turned because there the feature overheaded the town. And then as it turned it came under lateral fire from the direction of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, the terrain from your starting point in the direction of the Srdj feature, what are the topographical characteristics of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The terrain is open, rocky. There are no natural shelters, no possibilities of camouflage, and it is on an elevated position in respect to the position we were starting out from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you and your group went upwards, up the hill?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the tank also move up the hill up to the point you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Yes, the tank kept going up the hill throughout the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many troops were there in your group that headed out towards Srdj?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: Some 12 to 14 troops, including myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A minute ago you said that you came under fire as you were on the move. What did you do when you came under fire from the positions in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: When I came under fire from the direction of Dubrovnik, I asked my superior over the radio for the provision of support, that is to open fire at the mortar positions that were most -- that constituted the greatest threat for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fire that you requested, was it then opened on the positions that were endangering you?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The fire was not opened. I received a message from my commander, battalion commander Vladimir Kovacevic, that the fire group from the Uskoplje feature cannot open fire on the area of Babin Kuk, that is the area thereabouts, because they were out of range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pesic, what happened next? You were proceeding towards Srdj.

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: The moment I received the information that the battalion firing group cannot give us support by firing at the observed firing positions, and once I received information that it was not allowed for 130-millimetre guns to fire at these firing positions, I ordered my troops to accelerate our pace towards Srdj, because I calculated that as soon as we reach the feature, the mortars would stop firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps receive an order to suspend and abort your attack and return to your initial positions?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time during that day receive an order to abort the attack and another order instructing you to go back to your initial positions?

utterances.speaker: BUDIMIR PESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I -- by your leave, because we have another 20 minutes of examination, I would like to continue the examination of this witness tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now to resume at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of July, 2004, at 9.30 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.30 p.m.
